extensions - Search for VS Code extensions
getTaskOutput - Get Task Output
getTerminalOutput - Get Terminal Output
killTerminal - Kill Terminal
rename - Rename a symbol across the workspace
renderMermaidDiagram - Render a Mermaid.js diagram from markup.
report_customization_migration - Report Customization Migration
requires_confirmation_tool - Requires Confirmation Tool
runInTerminal - Run commands in the terminal
runTask - Run tasks in the workspace
sendToTerminal - Send to Terminal
terminalLastCommand - Get Terminal Last Command
terminalSelection - Get Terminal Selection
usages - Find references, definitions, and implementations of a symbol

description.value: Controls which tools are eligible for automatic approval. Tools set to 'false' will always present a confirmation and will never offer the option to auto-approve. The default behavior (or setting a tool to 'true') may result in the tool offering auto-approval options.

chat.artifacts.enabled.description: Controls whether the artifacts view is available in chat.

chat.artifacts.rules.byMimeType.description: Rules for extracting artifacts from tool results by MIME type. Maps MIME type patterns (e.g. 'image/*') to group configuration.

groupName.description: Display name for the artifact group.

onlyShowGroup.description: When true, show only the group header instead of individual items.

chat.artifacts.rules.byFilePath.description: Rules for extracting artifacts from written files by file path pattern. Maps glob patterns to group configuration.

groupName.description: Display name for the artifact group.

onlyShowGroup.description: When true, show only the group header instead of individual items.

chat.artifacts.rules.byMemoryFilePath.description: Rules for extracting artifacts from memory tool calls by memory file path pattern. Maps glob patterns to group configuration.

groupName.description: Display name for the artifact group.

onlyShowGroup.description: When true, show only the group header instead of individual items.

chat.undoRequests.restoreInput.markdownDescription: Controls whether the input of the chat should be restored when an undo request is made. The input will be filled with the text of the request that was restored.

chat.editRequests.markdownDescription: Enables editing of requests in the chat. This allows you to change the request content and resubmit it to the model.

chat.pasteAsAttachmentThreshold.markdownDescription: The number of characters a paste must exceed before it is added to the chat input as an attachment instead of being inserted inline. Set this to a very large number to always paste inline.

chat.viewSessions.enabled.description: Show chat agent sessions when chat is empty or to the side when chat view is wide enough.

enumDescriptions: Display chat sessions vertically stacked above the chat input unless a chat session is visible.
Display chat sessions side by side if space is sufficient, otherwise fallback to stacked above the chat input unless a chat session is visible.
chat.viewSessions.orientation.description: Controls the orientation of the chat agent sessions view when it is shown alongside the chat.

chat.viewProgressBadge.enabled.description: Show a progress badge on the chat view when an agent session is in progress that is opened in that view.

enumDescriptions: Use Archive, Archive All, Unarchive, and Unarchive All.
Use Mark as Done, Mark All as Done, Restore, and Restore All.
chat.experimental.sessionArchiveActionWo.description: Controls the wording and icons used by actions that archive and unarchive chat sessions, as well as the label of the archived sessions section.

enumDescriptions: Never show the handoff tip.
Show the handoff tip with the default description.
Show the handoff tip with an alternate description.
chat.agentsHandoffTip.mode.description: Controls the tip shown above the chat input offering to continue eligible agent sessions in the Agents Window.

chat.btwTip.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls whether the Agents Window shows a tip about using `/btw` to ask side questions.

chat.automateTip.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls whether the Agents Window shows a tip about using `/automate` to create recurring automations.

chat.sendInBackgroundTip.enabled.description: Controls whether the Agents Window shows a tip about starting new sessions in the background.

chat.editor.codex.preferAgentHost.markdownDescription: When enabled, Codex sessions opened from the regular workbench (sidebar chat) run inside the agent host process using the Codex App Server instead of the OpenAI extension. Only one Codex implementation surfaces per window. Requires `#chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled#`.

chat.contextUsage.enabled.description: Show the context window usage indicator in the chat input.

chat.verbose.description: Show request and completion timestamps. Hover over a completion timestamp to show the elapsed response time.

chat.progressBorder.enabled.markdownDescription: Show an animated gradient border around the chat input while the agent is working or thinking, instead of pinning persistent progress above the input when scrolling. When disabled, the indicator remains visible while scrolling if `#chat.persistentProgress#` is enabled. The border animation has no effect when reduced motion is enabled.

enumDescriptions: Keep the original thinking, tool, and working progress rendering without a persistent indicator or VS Code logo.
Tie the VS Code mark with fast parabolic ribbon motion, hold it, then unravel it before a brief rest.
Use the Draw animation with the same grayscale treatment as the VS Code icon in the Agents window. High contrast themes retain their contrast color.
Keep the same persistent progress text and tool rendering as Draw (Monochrome), but hide the VS Code icon.
chat.persistentProgress.markdownDescription: Keep a working progress indicator at the bottom until the response finishes, with a colored or monochrome Draw animation, or without an icon. The indicator reports running subagents and background commands from the current or earlier requests, even while the main response progresses. The default is Draw in all versions of VS Code. Experiments can override the default; an explicit setting takes precedence. Tool calls follow `#chat.persistentProgressVerbosity#`. Except in Conversation mode, reasoning is separated into collapsible previews that break the tool chain. Standalone tools retain their icons. Completed responses still follow `#chat.agent.collapseCompletedResponses#`. This replaces inner working progress; terminal activity animations and rich subagent pills are unchanged. Changes apply immediately; reduced motion keeps the indicator visible without animation.

enumDescriptions: Keep tool calls in expanded, headerless chains without an internal scrolling limit.
Preview tool calls while they run, then collapse each group to a single expandable summary row when the response moves on.

Collapse reasoning and tool calls together into a single section that names the current tool call or reasoning heading while it runs. Once it finishes, it shows what its tool calls did, followed by the time it took when known, or how long it thought when it has no tool calls.
chat.persistentProgressVerbosity.markdownDescription: Control tool call details when `#chat.persistentProgress#` is enabled. Compact is the default and collapses tool groups in place when thinking or response text resumes, or the response finishes. When Agent Host activity data is available, headers summarize up to three activity groups, prioritizing edits and commands, without language model requests. Remaining activity is counted as other steps. Failed, skipped, denied, and unfinished tool invocations remain explicit, including in the other-steps count. Completed shell invocations count as commands without tracking later background process status. Groups with no recognized activity or outcome use a step count. Expand a summary to inspect all its tool calls. Conversation collapses reasoning and tool calls between response text into one section that starts collapsed, names the current tool call, or the heading of the current reasoning summary (Thinking, followed by the first line of the reasoning on a single row, when the reasoning has no heading), while it runs. Once it finishes, its header shows what its tool calls did, such as how many commands ran and which files were read or edited, followed by the time its reasoning and tool calls took when all of it was recorded. A section without tool calls shows how long it thought instead. A finished section never uses a reasoning heading or a generated summary as its header. Inside a section with tool calls, each reasoning run is a collapsible row naming how long it thought. Has no effect when persistent progress is Off. Changes apply immediately.

chat.experimental.sessionStateIndicator..markdownDescription: Enable state indicators around chat editor sessions that are in progress, need attention, or have an unvisited completion. Customize the borders with `chat.sessionStateIndicator.inProgressBorder`, `chat.sessionStateIndicator.needsInputBorder`, and `chat.sessionStateIndicator.unvisitedBorder` in `#workbench.colorCustomizations#`.

enumDescriptions: Never show OS notifications for responses.
Show OS notifications for responses when the window is not focused.
Always show OS notifications for responses, even when the window is focused.
chat.notifyWindowOnResponseReceived.description: Controls whether a chat session should present the user with an OS notification when a response is received. This includes a window badge as well as notification toast.

chat.checkpoints.enabled.description: Enables checkpoints in chat. Checkpoints allow you to restore the chat to a previous state.

chat.checkpoints.showFileChanges.description: Controls whether to show chat checkpoint file changes.

chat.mcp.access.description: Controls access to installed Model Context Protocol servers.
enumDescriptions: No access to MCP servers.
Allows access to MCP servers listed in the registry that VS Code is connected to.
Allow access to any installed MCP server.

description.value: Controls access to installed Model Context Protocol servers.

enumDescriptions.value: No access to MCP servers.
Allows access to MCP servers listed in the registry that VS Code is connected to.
Allow access to any installed MCP server.

chat.mcp.autostart.description: Controls whether MCP servers should be automatically started when the chat messages are submitted.
enumDescriptions: Never automatically start MCP servers.
Only automatically start new MCP servers that have never been run.
Automatically start new and outdated MCP servers that are not yet running.

chat.mcp.apps.enabled.description: Controls whether MCP servers can provide custom UI for tool invocations.

chat.mcp.collisionBehavior.description: Controls behavior when multiple MCP servers are discovered with the same name. 'disable' disables lower-priority duplicates. 'suffix' appends numeric suffixes to disambiguate.
enumDescriptions: Disable lower-priority servers with duplicate names.
Append numeric suffixes to servers with duplicate names.

chat.mcp.serverSampling.description: Configures which models are exposed to MCP servers for sampling (making model requests in the background). This setting can be edited in a graphical way under the `MCP: List Servers` command.

allowedDuringChat.description: Whether this server is allowed to make sampling requests during its tool calls in a chat session.

allowedOutsideChat.description: Whether this server is allowed to make sampling requests outside of a chat session.

items.description: A model the MCP server has access to.

chat.mcp.assisted.nuget.enabled.description: Enables NuGet packages for AI-assisted MCP server installation. Used to install MCP servers by name from the central registry for .NET packages (NuGet.org).

chat.extensionTools.enabled.description: Enable using tools contributed by third-party extensions. These tools are also disabled when your organization disables MCP.

description.value: Enable using tools contributed by third-party extensions. These tools are also disabled when your organization disables MCP.

chat.plugins.enabled.description: Enable agent plugin integration in chat.

description.value: Enable agent plugin integration in chat.

chat.pluginLocations.markdownDescription: Plugin directories to discover. Each key is a path that points directly to a plugin folder, and the value enables (`true`) or disables (`false`) it. Paths can be absolute, relative to the workspace root, or start with `~/` for the user's home directory.

chat.plugins.enabledPlugins.markdownDescription: Controls which [agent plugins](https://aka.ms/vscode-agent-plugins) are enabled or disabled. Keys are plugin IDs in `<plugin>@<marketplace>` form (where marketplace is defined in `#chat.plugins.marketplaces#`); values enable (`true`) or disable (`false`) the plugin. Discovered alongside the path-keyed entries in `#chat.pluginLocations#`. When set by policy, entries are additive: plugins mapped to `true` are enabled in addition to the user's own plugins, and only plugins mapped to `false` are blocked from loading.

description.value: Plugin enablement. Keys are plugin IDs in `{plugin}@{marketplace}` form; values enable or disable the plugin.

chat.plugins.marketplaces.markdownDescription: Plugin marketplaces to query. Entries may be GitHub shorthand (`owner/repo` or `owner/repo#ref`), direct Git repository URIs (`https://...git`, `ssh://...git`, or `git@host:path.git`, each optionally suffixed with `#ref`), or local repository URIs (`file:///...`). Equivalent GitHub shorthand and URI entries are deduplicated.

chat.agent.enabled.description: When enabled, agent mode can be activated from chat and tools in agentic contexts with side effects can be used.

description.value: When enabled, agent mode can be activated from chat and tools in agentic contexts with side effects can be used.

chat.agent.networkFilter.markdownDescription:
When enabled, network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) is restricted according to `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains#` and `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains#`. Domain filtering is also applied to those tools when `#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#` is enabled.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

description.value:
When enabled, network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) is restricted according to `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains#` and `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains#`. Domain filtering is also applied to those tools when `#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#` is enabled.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomain.markdownDescription:
Allowed domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) when `#chat.agent.networkFilter#` is enabled. In Copilot Agent Host sessions with sandboxing (`#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#`) enabled, also restricts the integrated browser when outbound network access (`#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork#`) is allowed; an empty allow list adds no sandbox restriction. This list does not enable outbound access. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`. Outside sandboxing, when both allowed and denied lists are empty, all domains are blocked. Denied domains (see `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains#`) take precedence.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

description.value:
Allowed domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) when `#chat.agent.networkFilter#` is enabled. In Copilot Agent Host sessions with sandboxing (`#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#`) enabled, also restricts the integrated browser when outbound network access (`#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork#`) is allowed; an empty allow list adds no sandbox restriction. This list does not enable outbound access. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`. Outside sandboxing, when both allowed and denied lists are empty, all domains are blocked. Denied domains (see `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains#`) take precedence.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains.markdownDescription:
Denied domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) when `#chat.agent.networkFilter#` is enabled. Also applies to the integrated browser in sandboxed Copilot Agent Host sessions (`#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#`); allowing outbound network access (`#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork#`) does not bypass this list. Takes precedence over `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains#`. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

description.value:
Denied domains for network access by agent tools (fetch tool, integrated browser) when `#chat.agent.networkFilter#` is enabled. Also applies to the integrated browser in sandboxed Copilot Agent Host sessions (`#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#`); allowing outbound network access (`#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork#`) does not bypass this list. Takes precedence over `#chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains#`. Supports wildcards like `*.example.com`.

Changes may not take full effect until VS Code is restarted.

chat.newSession.defaultMode.description: The default mode for new chat sessions. When empty, the chat view's default mode is used.

chat.agentHost.debugLogs.defaultExportLo.patternErrorMessage: The default Agent Host debug-log export location must be an absolute path (for example, C:\\myFolder or /myFolder).
chat.agentHost.debugLogs.defaultExportLo.description: The default folder for archives and folders created by the Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs command. When empty or unavailable, the default file-dialog location is used.

chat.agentHost.agentDebugLog.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable agent debug logging for agent host sessions: surface their debug events in the agent debug panel. Takes effect immediately; only sessions that run while this is enabled are captured.

chat.agentHost.agentDebugLog.maxEventsIn.markdownDescription: Maximum number of debug events kept in memory per agent host session for the agent debug panel. Older events beyond this limit are dropped from the in-memory buffer, which also lowers the totals (such as token usage) shown in the panel overview.

chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enable.description: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions use the Agent Host terminal tool override instead of the SDK's default terminal behavior. Not supported on Windows, where sessions use the SDK's terminal and sandbox runtime.

description.value: Enable the Agent Host custom terminal tool override for Copilot SDK sessions.

chat.agentHost.shellTool.initScript.enab.markdownDescription: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions load your shell profile (`~/.bashrc` on macOS and Linux, PowerShell profiles on Windows) and activate the Python environment selected for the workspace before each shell command. Python activation requires the Python Environments extension with `#python-envs.terminal.autoActivationType#` set to `shellStartup`. Local windows only.

enumDescriptions: Log informational messages. Running VS Code with trace logging still enables all Copilot SDK runtime diagnostics.
Log all Copilot SDK runtime diagnostics.
chat.agentHost.copilotSdk.logLevel.markdownDescription: Controls the log level for the Copilot SDK runtime used by the local agent host. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client; active sessions are reloaded when next used.

chat.agentHost.copilot.policyHelper.markdownDescription: Policy helper executable for the local Copilot runtime, with an absolute `path` and optional `args`. Device and server policies take precedence. This advanced setting is omitted from Settings JSON suggestions. Changes restart the Copilot SDK client after active turns and subagents finish. Helper script content changes do not trigger a restart.

chat.copilot.claudeAdvisor.enabled.markdownDescription: When enabled, Copilot Agent Host sessions using a supported Claude model can call the provider-native Advisor tool. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish.

chat.copilot.searchSubagent.enabled.markdownDescription: When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions are offered the Copilot runtime's search subagent tool for codebase search. Applies to sessions when they launch or resume.

chat.copilot.searchSubagent.grepNudge.en.markdownDescription: When enabled, Copilot Agent Host defers at most one grep search per user message during the first two user messages when the search subagent is enabled and available. Further grep calls proceed through normal permissions without another nudge. Does not affect searches inside subagents.

chat.copilot.searchSubagent.model.markdownDescription: CAPI model ID to use for the search subagent in local Copilot Agent Host sessions when `#chat.copilot.searchSubagent.enabled#` is enabled. Empty uses the runtime default. An unavailable model makes the search tool unavailable. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish.

chat.copilot.exploreAgent.enabled.markdownDescription: When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions can use the runtime's built-in Explore agent, independently of `#chat.copilot.searchSubagent.enabled#`. Applies to sessions when they launch or resume. Does not disable custom agents named Explore.

chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.markdownDescription: When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions opt into the Copilot runtime's execution subagent. The runtime's experiment assignments may override this default. When the runtime implementation is available, the extension-native execution tool is excluded from that session. This is independent of `#github.copilot.chat.executionSubagent.enabled#`, which controls the extension-native implementation. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot runtime after active turns finish.

Default model ID for the Copilot runtime's execution subagent. Empty inherits the parent session model. The runtime's experiment assignments may override this default. This does not affect the extension-native execution subagent's model. An unavailable model disables the runtime execution subagent. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot runtime after active turns finish.

chat.agentHost.opus48Prompt.enabled.description: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions running a Claude Opus 4.8 model apply Opus 4.8-tuned system-prompt section overrides on top of the default system message.

chat.copilot.stabilityOrderedPrompt.enab.description: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions order the system prompt by how often each section changes, so sessions with the same tools and workspace can reuse each other's prompt cache. This moves per-session sections, such as the environment and session folder, to the end of the system prompt. Applies to new and resumed sessions.

chat.agentHost.copilot.progressUpdatesPr.description: When enabled, Copilot SDK sessions running a GPT model or Auto are asked to send a brief user-visible update before their first tool call and while they work. Applies to new and resumed sessions.

chat.agentHost.copilot.includeCoAuthored.markdownDescription: Controls whether Copilot Agent Host sessions, such as those in the Agents window, add a `Co-authored-by: Copilot` trailer to the commits they create. Takes effect when a session starts or resumes.

chat.agentHost.copilot.shellAuthenticati.markdownDescription: Controls whether Copilot Agent Host sessions ask in chat for the passwords, passphrases, and confirmations that `sudo -A`, `ssh`, and `git` request. The answer goes only to that program and isn't sent to the model. Takes effect when a session starts or resumes.

chat.copilot.skillCharBudget.description: Maximum number of characters available for skill descriptions in the Copilot SDK system message.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Agents cannot generate or edit images.

Generate and edit images with **GPT Image 2.5 Flare** when it is available to your account. Prompts and selected images are sent to Flare.

**Preview rates (AI credits per 1 million tokens):**
- **Text tokens:** 500 input / 0 output
- **Image tokens:** 800 input / 3,000 output

These charges are in addition to the conversation model. Rates may change; these are token rates, not per-image prices.
chat.copilot.imageGeneration.model.markdownDescription: Selects the model Copilot uses to generate and edit images, or turns image generation off. Each model lists its rates. Account access and tool permissions still apply, and choosing **Off** prevents future image tool calls.

chat.copilot.imageGeneration.watermark.markdownDescription: Request a visible "Made with AI" label on images generated or edited by Copilot. Applies to new and existing Copilot sessions without enabling image generation. Labels are generated by the image model and are not guaranteed. Turning this off does not remove existing labels from input images.

chat.copilot.localModel.enabled.description: When enabled, offers on-device models to download and run on this device with llama.cpp. Offered only on devices with a GPU that has about 64 GB of memory or more. Changing this setting restarts the local Copilot runtime after active turns finish. Local models may not use the same safety filters as GitHub Copilot-provided models and may be more susceptible to malicious instructions, especially when actions are automatically approved.

chat.copilot.localModel.useInAuto.description: When enabled, Auto can route turns to the active on-device model, with cloud fallback. Takes effect immediately. Local models may not use the same safety filters as GitHub Copilot-provided models and may be more susceptible to malicious instructions, especially when actions are automatically approved.

chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a `llama-server` executable for on-device models. VS Code doesn't install llama.cpp: install a build that supports your model, then set this to its `llama-server`.

chat.copilot.memory.local.enabled.markdownDescription: When enabled, local Copilot Agent Host sessions store [Copilot Memory](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory) in the repository's `.github/copilot-memories.jsonl` file instead of GitHub's cloud memory service. The file is part of the working tree, so commits made by the agent or the Agents window can include it. Requires a GitHub-hosted repository. **Note:** your Copilot Memory settings and organization policies on GitHub don't apply, and user-scoped memories are unavailable. Changing this setting restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish.

enumDescriptions: Place retrieved memories in the system prompt.
Place retrieved memories in generated user messages instead of the system prompt.
chat.copilot.memory.mode.markdownDescription: Controls where Copilot Agent Host sessions place retrieved [Copilot Memory](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory) when sending a request to the model. Applies to new and resumed sessions.

github.copilot.chat.autoModeTierOverride.markdownDescription: Override Auto's "Optimize for" preference for evals and debugging. Accepts `efficiency`, `balance`, or `intelligence` in both Copilot Chat and Copilot SDK sessions; `fast` is extension-only. Set to `null` to clear.

chat.agentHost.copilot.modelCapabilityOv.markdownDescription: Per-model overrides for Copilot Agent Host sessions. Use `*` to match every model. Supports model family, reasoning effort, tool filters, model capabilities, and YAML prompt overrides.

family.description: Route the model to another family's tuned system prompt and tool profile (e.g. `claude-opus-4.8`). The model id sent to the runtime is unaffected, so the session still runs on the selected model.

reasoningEffort.description: Reasoning effort for sessions on this model, overriding the model picker's effort level. Use the `*` entry to set it for every model. Unrecognized values are ignored.

availableTools.description: When set, only matching tools are available to sessions on this model. Patterns: bare tool names, `builtin:*` or `builtin:<name>` (Copilot runtime tools), `mcp:*` or `mcp:<name>` (MCP server tools), and `custom:*` or `custom:<name>` (every tool VS Code registers with the SDK, including the agent host's own terminal tools); a bare `*` expands to all three sources.

excludedTools.description: Tools disabled for sessions on this model; same pattern syntax as `availableTools` and takes precedence over it. Note that `custom:*` and a bare `*` also disable the agent host's own terminal tools registered with the SDK.

modelCapabilities.description: Per-property model capability overrides passed through to the Copilot SDK's `modelCapabilities` session field (e.g. `{ "supports": { "vision": false }, "limits": { "max_context_window_tokens": 64000 } }`), deep-merged over the runtime's resolved defaults for this model. Applied when the session launches or resumes.

promptOverrideString.description: Inline YAML containing `systemPrompt` and/or `toolDescriptions` overrides. Takes precedence over `promptOverrideFile`. A system prompt replaces all Agent Host and SDK prompt sections and guardrails.

promptOverrideFile.description: Path to a YAML file containing `systemPrompt` and/or `toolDescriptions` overrides. Ignored when `promptOverrideString` is configured.

enumDescriptions: Offer "Continue with Microsoft" only when a Microsoft work or school account on this device is linked to a GitHub account. This is checked silently in the background: Microsoft may record a sign-in, and the GitHub access used for the check is revoked when possible.
Always offer "Continue with Microsoft", without checking for a linked account.
Never offer "Continue with Microsoft", and never check for a linked account.
chat.microsoftAuthentication.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls when sign-in surfaces, such as the sign-in dialog and the welcome screen, offer "Continue with Microsoft". Signing in with Microsoft exchanges your Microsoft account for the GitHub access your organization has linked to it. The resulting GitHub sign-in lasts for the current window session only and is not saved.

chat.tools.confirmationCarousel.enabled.description: When enabled, tool confirmations are shown in a carousel above the input, including confirmations from subagents and earlier responses.

chat.tools.riskAssessment.enabled.description: When enabled, tool confirmations show an LLM-generated risk level (Safe / Caution / Review carefully) and a short explanation.

chat.tools.riskAssessment.model.description: The language model id used to generate tool risk assessments. Should be a small, fast model.

chat.planAgent.defaultModel.description: Select the default language model to use for the Plan agent from the available providers.

chat.exploreAgent.defaultModel.description: Select the default language model to use for the Explore subagent from the available providers.

chat.byokUtilityModelDefault.markdownDescription: Controls the default model used by built-in utility flows when the selected main agent model is a bring your own key (BYOK) model. This setting has no effect when the selected main agent model is provided by GitHub Copilot. A specific model configured in `#chat.utilityModel#` or `#chat.utilitySmallModel#` takes precedence.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Do not use a default utility model.
Use the selected BYOK main agent model.
Use the default GitHub Copilot utility models.

chat.utilityModel.description: Override the language model used by built-in utility flows. Leave empty to use the configured default behavior.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Use the default behavior for utility models

chat.utilitySmallModel.description: Override the language model used by built-in small/fast utility flows. A fast and inexpensive model is recommended. Leave empty to use the configured default behavior.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Use the default behavior for utility models

enumDescriptions: Queue the message to send after the current request completes.
Steer the current request by sending the message immediately, signaling the current request to yield.
chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction.description: Controls which action is the default for the queue button when a request is in progress.

chat.math.enabled.description: Enable math rendering in chat responses using KaTeX.

chat.htmlPreview.enabled.description: Render explicit html-preview code blocks as inline HTML previews in the Agents window. When disabled, these blocks are shown as source code.

chat.nativeComponents.enabled.description: Render explicit vscode-ui code blocks as native visuals, such as metrics, tables, and bar charts, in Agents window responses. When disabled, these blocks are shown as source code.

chat.agent.codeBlockProgress.description: When applying edits, show a progress animation in the code block pill. If disabled, shows the progress percentage instead.

copilot.description: GitHub Copilot CLI configuration (`mcp-config.json` in `COPILOT_HOME`, or `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` when unset)

chat.mcp.discovery.enabled.markdownDescription: Configures discovery of Model Context Protocol servers from configuration from various other applications. The GitHub Copilot CLI configuration is discovered by default; other applications must be enabled explicitly.

chat.mcp.workspaceRootConfig.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer the workspace root `.mcp.json` file when adding MCP servers manually. When `.vscode/mcp.json` exists, choose which file to add to. Marketplace installations continue to use `.vscode/mcp.json`. Existing `.mcp.json` files can be opened and read independently of this setting.

chat.instructionsFilesLocations.title: Instructions File Locations
chat.instructionsFilesLocations.markdownDescription:
Specify location(s) of instructions files (`*.instructions.md`) that can be attached in Chat sessions. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-custom-instructions).

Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace.

Locations configured here are only observed by the Local agent harness. Other harnesses running in VS Code receive instructions from all additional locations configured here, in addition to their built-in locations. To use instructions with independent agent harnesses, such as Copilot CLI, review the [Migrations tab](command:aiCustomization.openManagementEditor?%255B%257B%2522migration%2522%253Atrue%257D%255D "Open the Migrations Tab") in the Agent Customizations editor to migrate them to supported locations.

propertyNames.patternErrorMessage: Paths must be relative or start with '~/'. Absolute paths and '\' separators are not supported. Glob patterns are deprecated and will be removed in future versions.

chat.promptFilesLocations.deprecationMessage: This setting and the Local agent harness will be removed in a future release. Review the Migrations tab in the Agent Customizations editor to convert prompt files into skills.
chat.promptFilesLocations.title: Prompt File Locations
chat.promptFilesLocations.markdownDescription:
Specify location(s) of reusable prompt files (`*.prompt.md`) that can be run in Chat sessions. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-prompt-snippets).

Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace.

This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.
chat.promptFilesLocations.markdownDeprecationMessage: This setting and the Local agent harness will be removed in a future release. Review the [Migrations tab](command:aiCustomization.openManagementEditor?%255B%257B%2522migration%2522%253Atrue%257D%255D "Open the Migrations Tab") in the Agent Customizations editor to convert prompt files into skills.

propertyNames.patternErrorMessage: Paths must be relative or start with '~/'. Absolute paths and '\' separators are not supported. Glob patterns are deprecated and will be removed in future versions.

chat.modeFilesLocations.deprecationMessage: This setting and the Local agent harness will be removed in a future release. Chat modes are now called custom agents and are located in .github/agents. Review the Migrations tab in the Agent Customizations editor to move them into supported locations.
chat.modeFilesLocations.title: Mode File Locations
chat.modeFilesLocations.markdownDescription:
Specify location(s) of custom chat mode files (`*.chatmode.md`). [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-custom-chat-modes).

Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace.

This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.
chat.modeFilesLocations.markdownDeprecationMessage: This setting and the Local agent harness will be removed in a future release. Chat modes are now called custom agents and are located in `.github/agents`. Review the [Migrations tab](command:aiCustomization.openManagementEditor?%255B%257B%2522migration%2522%253Atrue%257D%255D "Open the Migrations Tab") in the Agent Customizations editor to move them into supported locations.

chat.agentFilesLocations.title: Agent File Locations
chat.agentFilesLocations.markdownDescription:
Specify location(s) of custom agent files (`*.agent.md`). [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-ghcp-custom-chat-modes).

Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace.

Locations configured here are only observed by the Local agent harness. Other harnesses running in VS Code receive agents from all additional locations configured here, in addition to their built-in locations. To use agents with independent agent harnesses, such as Copilot CLI, review the [Migrations tab](command:aiCustomization.openManagementEditor?%255B%257B%2522migration%2522%253Atrue%257D%255D "Open the Migrations Tab") in the Agent Customizations editor to migrate them to supported locations.

propertyNames.patternErrorMessage: Paths must be relative or start with '~/'. Absolute paths and '\' separators are not supported.

chat.useAgentsMdFile.title: Use AGENTS.md file
chat.useAgentsMdFile.markdownDescription: Controls whether instructions from `AGENTS.md` file found in a workspace roots are attached to all chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.useNestedAgentsMdFiles.title: Use nested AGENTS.md files
chat.useNestedAgentsMdFiles.markdownDescription: Controls whether instructions from nested `AGENTS.md` files found in the workspace are listed in all chat requests. The language model can load these skills on-demand if the `read` tool is available. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.useClaudeMdFile.title: Use CLAUDE.md file
chat.useClaudeMdFile.markdownDescription: Controls whether instructions from `CLAUDE.md` file found in workspace roots, .claude and ~/.claude folder are attached to all chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.useAgentSkills.title: Use Agent skills
chat.useAgentSkills.markdownDescription: Controls whether skills are provided as specialized capabilities to the chat requests. Skills are loaded from the folders configured in `#chat.agentSkillsLocations#`. The language model can load these skills on-demand if the `read` tool is available. Learn more about [Agent Skills](https://aka.ms/vscode-agent-skills). This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.experimental.useSkillAdherencePromp.title: Use Skill Adherence Prompt
chat.experimental.useSkillAdherencePromp.markdownDescription: Controls whether a stronger skill adherence prompt is used that encourages the model to immediately invoke skills when relevant rather than just announcing them. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.includeApplyingInstructions.title: Include Applying Instructions
chat.includeApplyingInstructions.markdownDescription: Controls whether instructions with a matching 'applyTo' attribute are automatically included in chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.includeReferencedInstructions.title: Include Referenced Instructions
chat.includeReferencedInstructions.markdownDescription: Controls whether referenced instructions are automatically included in chat requests. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.useCustomizationsInParentRepositori.title: Use Customizations in Parent Repositories
chat.useCustomizationsInParentRepositori.markdownDescription: Controls whether to use chat customization files in parent repositories. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.agentSkillsLocations.title: Agent Skills Locations
chat.agentSkillsLocations.markdownDescription:
Specify location(s) of agent skills (`SKILL.md`) that can be used in Chat Sessions. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-agent-skills).

Each path should contain skill subfolders with SKILL.md files (e.g., add `my-skills` if you have `my-skills/skillA/SKILL.md`). Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace.

Locations configured here are only observed by the Local agent harness. Other harnesses running in VS Code receive skills from all additional locations configured here, in addition to their built-in locations. To use skills with independent agent harnesses, such as Copilot CLI, review the [Migrations tab](command:aiCustomization.openManagementEditor?%255B%257B%2522migration%2522%253Atrue%257D%255D "Open the Migrations Tab") in the Agent Customizations editor to migrate them to supported locations.

propertyNames.patternErrorMessage: Paths must be relative or start with '~/'. Absolute paths and '\' separators are not supported.

chat.hookFilesLocations.title: Hook File Locations
chat.hookFilesLocations.markdownDescription:
Specify paths to hook configuration files that define custom shell commands to execute at strategic points in an agent's workflow. [Learn More](https://aka.ms/vscode-chat-hooks).

Relative paths are resolved from the root folder(s) of your workspace. Supports Copilot hooks (`*.json`) and Claude Code hooks (`settings.json`, `settings.local.json`).

This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

propertyNames.patternErrorMessage: Paths must be relative or start with '~/'. Absolute paths and '\' separators are not supported.

chat.useHooks.title: Use Chat Hooks
chat.useHooks.markdownDescription: Controls whether chat hooks are executed at strategic points during an agent's workflow. Hooks are loaded from the files configured in `#chat.hookFilesLocations#`. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

description.value: Controls whether chat hooks are executed at strategic points during an agent's workflow. Hooks are loaded from the files configured in `#chat.hookFilesLocations#`. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.useClaudeHooks.title: Use Claude Hooks
chat.useClaudeHooks.markdownDescription: Controls whether hooks from Claude configuration files can execute. When disabled, only Copilot-format hooks are used. Hooks are loaded from the files configured in `#chat.hookFilesLocations#`. This setting is only used by the Local agent harness.

chat.promptFilesRecommendations.title: Prompt File Recommendations
chat.promptFilesRecommendations.markdownDescription: Configure which prompt files to recommend in the chat welcome view. Each key is a prompt file name, and the value can be `true` to always recommend, `false` to never recommend, or a [when clause](https://aka.ms/vscode-when-clause) expression like `resourceExtname == .js` or `resourceLangId == markdown`.

chat.tools.todos.showWidget.description: Controls whether to show the todo list widget above the chat input. When enabled, the widget displays todo items created by the agent and updates as progress is made.

chat.agent.thinkingStyle.deprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use chat.persistentProgress and chat.persistentProgressVerbosity to control thinking and progress presentation instead.
enumDescriptions: Thinking parts will be collapsed by default.
Thinking parts will be expanded first, then collapse once we reach a part that is not thinking.
Show thinking in a fixed-height streaming panel that auto-scrolls; click header to expand to full height.
chat.agent.thinkingStyle.description: Controls how thinking is rendered. Read-only chats always use the collapsed preview style.
chat.agent.thinkingStyle.markdownDeprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use `#chat.persistentProgress#` and `#chat.persistentProgressVerbosity#` to control thinking and progress presentation instead.

chat.agent.thinking.generateTitles.description: Generate a summary only when a live thinking section finishes with its header in view. A single extracted reasoning heading is used directly without a model request; multiple headings are used as summary input. Opening a chat, returning to it, scrolling or expanding existing sections never generates titles. Sections that finish off-screen or in background chats keep their existing title or Finished thinking. Conversation sections never use a reasoning heading or a generated summary as their title.

chat.agent.thinking.collapsedTools.deprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use chat.persistentProgress and chat.persistentProgressVerbosity to control thinking and progress presentation instead.
enumDescriptions: Tool calls are shown separately, not collapsed into thinking.
Tool calls are collapsed into thinking sections when thinking is present.
Tool calls are always collapsed, even without thinking.
chat.agent.thinking.collapsedTools.markdownDescription: Controls how tool calls are displayed in relation to thinking sections.
chat.agent.thinking.collapsedTools.markdownDeprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use `#chat.persistentProgress#` and `#chat.persistentProgressVerbosity#` to control thinking and progress presentation instead.

chat.agent.thinking.terminalTools.deprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use chat.persistentProgress and chat.persistentProgressVerbosity to control thinking and progress presentation instead.
chat.agent.thinking.terminalTools.markdownDescription: When enabled, terminal tool calls are displayed inside the thinking dropdown with a simplified view.
chat.agent.thinking.terminalTools.markdownDeprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use `#chat.persistentProgress#` and `#chat.persistentProgressVerbosity#` to control thinking and progress presentation instead.

chat.agent.thinking.phrases.deprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use chat.persistentProgress and chat.persistentProgressVerbosity to control thinking and progress presentation instead.

mode.description: 'replace' replaces all default phrases entirely; 'append' adds your phrases to all default categories.

phrases.description: Custom loading messages to show during thinking, working progress, terminal, and tool operations.

chat.agent.thinking.phrases.markdownDescription: Customize the loading messages shown during agent thinking and progress indicators. Use `"mode": "replace"` to use only your phrases, or `"mode": "append"` to add them to the defaults.
chat.agent.thinking.phrases.markdownDeprecationMessage: This setting will be deprecated in a future release. Use `#chat.persistentProgress#` and `#chat.persistentProgressVerbosity#` to control thinking and progress presentation instead.

chat.tools.terminal.simpleCollapsible.markdownDescription: When enabled, terminal tool calls are always displayed in a collapsible container with a simplified view.

chat.tools.terminal.outputReflow.description: Controls whether terminal output in chat reflows to fit the available width. When disabled, previews use the terminal's column count, or 80 columns when no terminal is available, and scroll horizontally when needed. This does not resize the terminal running the command.

chat.tools.compressOutput.enabled.markdownDescription: Post-process tool output (for example `git diff`, `ls -l`, or `npm install`) to reduce token usage before it is sent to the model.

chat.tools.autoExpandFailures.markdownDescription: When enabled, terminal tool failures are automatically expanded in the chat UI to show error details.

chat.disableAIFeatures.description: Disable and hide built-in AI features provided by GitHub Copilot, including chat and inline suggestions.

chat.copilotCliCommand.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls whether integrated terminals include the `copilot` command that ships with VS Code. The command runs GitHub Copilot CLI and offers to install it when it's missing. A GitHub Copilot CLI that you installed yourself isn't affected.

description.value: Controls whether VS Code provides the copilot command for GitHub Copilot CLI. When disabled, VS Code setup on Windows and the Linux DEB and RPM packages don't add the command to PATH and remove the entry they added, VS Code doesn't install GitHub Copilot CLI, and integrated terminals don't include the command. A GitHub Copilot CLI that was installed separately isn't affected.

chat.titleBar.signIn.enabled.description: Controls whether the Copilot Sign In button is shown in the title bar when signed out. When disabled, the Sign In affordance falls back to the status bar.

chat.welcomePage.signIn.enabled.description: Controls whether the Welcome page shows a GitHub sign-in button instead of the Agents window button when signed out.

enumDescriptions: Show no graphic.
Show the editor window and the Agents window side by side.
Show how editor windows for several projects become one Agents window.
Show 'manyWindowsToOne' when more than one editor window is open, and 'windowComparison' otherwise.
chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic.description: Controls which graphic explains the Agents window above the Agents window button on the Welcome page.

enumDescriptions: Don't set the section apart.
Show the section on a subtle surface, like the walkthrough tiles.
Outline the section with a subtle border.
Show the section on a surface tinted with the accent color.
Show the section on a subtle surface across the width of the page's content.
Separate the section from the rest of the page with lines above and below it.
chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowSectionStyl.description: Controls how the Agents window graphic, its captions and the Agents window button are set apart from the rest of the Welcome page. Applies only while a graphic is shown.

chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.enabled.description: Controls whether the Open in Agents Window button is shown in the title bar.

enumDescriptions: Show a simple tooltip, and grow the button to show its label.
Show a hover card with a graphic of editor windows for several projects becoming one Agents window, and keep the button an icon.
Show a hover card with a graphic of the editor window and the Agents window side by side, and keep the button an icon.
chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.richHov.description: Controls whether hovering or focusing the Open in Agents Window button in the title bar shows a hover card that explains the Agents window, and which graphic the card shows. Applies to users who have created fewer than two sessions in the Agents window; other users always see a simple tooltip.

chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.richHov.markdownDescription: Controls whether clicking the Open in Agents Window button in the title bar opens its hover card, with focus in it, instead of the Agents window. The card's Open Agents Window button opens the Agents window. Applies only while the button shows a hover card, see `#chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.richHover#`.

chat.agentsWindowBanner.enabled.description: Show occasional invitations to continue or manage running Agent Host chats in the Agents Window. Invitations are hidden for users who have created at least three sessions in the Agents Window and created their latest session within the past 30 days.

chat.agentsWindowBanner.developerMode.description: Preview one Agents Window invitation per window reload, ignoring experiment enablement, previous dismissals, frequency limits, and Agents Window usage. Activity requirements and delays still apply. Previews do not update invitation history or experiment telemetry.

chat.agentsWindowBanner.revealCurrentSes.markdownDescription: Open the invited chat when using an Agents Window invitation. When disabled, show the New Session view instead. When `#onboarding.enabled#` is enabled, highlight the invited session in the sessions list, followed by the New Session button if this setting is enabled.

chat.experimental.openInAgentsWindow.tra.description: Copy the prompt and attachments from a new chat when explicitly opening the new-session view in the Agents Window. Existing drafts in the Agents Window are preserved.

chat.agentsParallelWorkBanner.enabled.description: Show an invitation to work in parallel in the Agents Window when starting a new Agent Host chat while another Agent Host session is running.

enumDescriptions: Do not show the Copilot harness introduction.
Show the introduction when a new Copilot harness session starts.
Show the introduction after the first request is submitted in a new Copilot harness session.
chat.copilotHarnessIntroduction.mode.description: Controls when the introduction to the new Copilot experience is shown.

chat.harnessSwitchFeedbackSurvey.enabled.description: Show a one-time feedback survey after switching from Copilot to Local.

chat.agentsHandoffTip.delaySeconds.deprecationMessage: Agents Window invitation delays are now controlled independently for each scenario.
chat.agentsHandoffTip.delaySeconds.markdownDescription: Controls the delay, in seconds, after the latest user message before offering to continue an in-progress session in the Agents Window. Requires `#chat.agentsHandoffTip.mode#` to be `default` or `custom`.

chat.growthNotification.enabled.description: Controls whether to show a growth notification in the agent sessions view to encourage new users to try Copilot.

enumDescriptions: Do not show a promo on the Copilot icon when Chat is closed.

Show a promo tooltip when hovering or clicking the Copilot status icon while Chat is closed. Viewing the offer clears its indicator; the offer remains available for the current window session. Choosing Try dismisses the offer and its chat banner.
chat.closedPromoNotification.description: Controls whether a live model promo is shown on the Copilot icon when Chat is closed. When explicitly set, this overrides the experiment without an experiment lookup. Otherwise, eligible promos use the experiment treatment.

chat.restoreLastPanelSession.description: Controls whether the last session is restored in panel after restart.

chat.exitAfterDelegation.description: Controls whether the chat panel automatically exits after delegating a request to another session.

chat.extensionUnification.enabled.description: Enables the unification of GitHub Copilot extensions. When enabled, all GitHub Copilot functionality is served from the GitHub Copilot Chat extension. When disabled, the GitHub Copilot and GitHub Copilot Chat extensions operate independently.

chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubag.markdownDescription: Controls whether subagents can invoke other subagents. When enabled, nesting is limited to a maximum depth of 5.

chat.subagents.showCreditUsage.description: Controls whether AI credit usage is shown next to the duration for subagents.

chat.terminal.agentHost.enabled.description: Controls whether Terminal Chat is backed by the Agent Host instead of the extension host. Applied on startup.

chat.inlineChat.agentHost.enabled.description: Controls whether editor inline chat is backed by the Agent Host instead of the extension host. Applied on startup.

chat.experimental.collectInstructionsInE.description: When enabled, automatic instruction collection (.instructions.md, agent instructions, customizations index) is performed by the GitHub Copilot Chat extension instead of the core workbench.

enumDescriptions: Use the default location for the window and sidebar layout.
Below the Sessions view in the Agents window. Uses the Chat toolbar in editor windows.
At the top left of the Sessions view in the Agents window. Uses the Chat toolbar in editor windows.
In the Chat toolbar.
Inside the chat input, after the model pickers and before the voice controls.
chat.customizations.location.description: Controls where the Customizations button appears. Explicit choices override the default location.

chat.customizations.structuredPreview.en.description: Controls whether the Chat Customizations editor shows a structured preview for markdown customization files (agents, skills, instructions, prompts). When disabled, the editor always opens the raw markdown in the embedded code editor.

chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled.description: Shows Browse instead of Overview when a customization marketplace source is enabled. When disabled, marketplace discovery remains in the existing customization management pages.

description.value: Shows Browse instead of Overview when a customization marketplace source is enabled. When disabled, marketplace discovery remains in the existing customization management pages.

chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.en.description: Enables Copilot connectors in the unified marketplace and exposes connected connector MCP servers in Chat Customizations and Copilot agent sessions.

description.value: Enables Copilot connectors in the unified marketplace and exposes connected connector MCP servers in Chat Customizations and Copilot agent sessions.

chat.customizations.marketplace.sources..description: Enables the SDK-backed GitHub Feed for agent harnesses that provide marketplace search. Local does not provide this source. If Marketplace or this setting is disabled, or a strict marketplace policy is configured, the GitHub Feed is not queried.

chat.customizations.promptMigration.enab.description: Controls whether the Chat Customizations editor offers to convert prompt files into skills for agent-host harnesses, which ignore prompt files. When disabled, the migration card and sidebar shortcut are hidden.

chat.customizations.migration.enabled.description: Controls whether VS Code shows customization migration actions, hints, compatibility badges, and compatibility details for the active Agent Host harness.

chat.customizations.userDataMigration.en.description: Controls whether the Chat Customizations editor offers to move agents and instructions stored in user data to the active agent-host harness, which ignores the user data location. When disabled, the migration card and sidebar shortcut are hidden.

chat.customizations.locationsMigration.e.description: Controls whether the Chat Customizations editor offers to move agents, instructions, and skills from configured locations that are not supported by the active agent-host harness. When disabled, the migration card and sidebar shortcut are hidden.

chat.customizations.mcpServerMigration.e.description: Controls whether VS Code shows MCP server migration actions, hints, compatibility badges, and compatibility details. Migration moves eligible workspace MCP servers out of .vscode/mcp.json and into a .mcp.json file at the workspace root, where the active agent-host harness discovers them directly.

enumDescriptions: Allow remote connections through a secure Dev Tunnel from VS Code or a browser.

Register this machine as a GitHub environment for remote agent access (preview). Remote clients receive trusted-owner access to sessions, tools, and workspace resources. Session actions are mirrored to GitHub for catalog and history storage. Conversation content is not end-to-end encrypted.
chat.agentHost.remoteConnections.description: Choose the connection method used by Allow Remote Connections. Selecting a method in the Remote Connections menu updates this setting and enables sharing. Selecting Off disables sharing without changing the preferred method. Changing this setting directly turns sharing off.

chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled.description: Enable connecting to remote agent hosts.

address.description: The WebSocket address of the remote agent host (e.g. "localhost:3000").

name.description: A display name for this remote agent host.

connectionToken.description: An optional connection token for authenticating with the remote agent host.

chat.workspaceRemoteAgentHosts.markdownDescription: WebSocket remote agent hosts that editor windows connect to while this workspace is open. Their agents become available in Chat, and their sessions are listed there. Editor windows don't connect to the hosts in `#chat.remoteAgentHosts#`; those belong to the Agents window. Only applies in trusted workspaces; connected hosts receive your GitHub credentials, so only list hosts you trust.

chat.agentHost.githubEnvironments.enable.description: Enable sharing this machine as a GitHub environment and discovering and connecting to your other shared machines through Mission Control.

description.value: Controls whether this machine can be shared as a GitHub environment and connect to other shared machines through Mission Control.

chat.agentHost.defaultCloneDirectory.markdownDescription: Root folder for repositories cloned by remote clients when this machine is shared as a GitHub environment. Repositories are cloned into `<root>/<owner>/<repository>`. Use an absolute path or a path starting with `~` for the local user's home folder. The folder is created if needed. When empty, falls back to `#git.defaultCloneDirectory#`, then the home folder. Changes apply to future clones and do not move existing repositories.

chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionContro.description: Use this host's GitHub and Copilot credentials for Mission Control sessions, including repository operations and restored background work, instead of the remote client's credentials. Remote clients must still authenticate as the same GitHub account. Requests use the host account's permissions and usage allowance. Changing this setting disconnects existing Mission Control clients.

chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.enabled.description: Use GitHub Cloud for new Cloud sessions in the Agents Window instead of Copilot coding agent on GitHub Actions. Also enables discovering and opening GitHub Cloud sessions.

chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.autoConnectO.description: Automatically connect to or wake a cloud sandbox environment in the background when opening or restoring its chat in the Agents Window. When disabled, connecting waits until you start composing or explicitly connect.

chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.earlyPrepara.description: Prepare an eligible cloud environment while typing in a new Cloud chat in the editor or Agents Window. This can allocate cloud compute before you send a message.

chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.sessionFeed..description: Try Mission Control push notifications to discover and refresh cloud sandbox sessions when enabled for your GitHub account. If unavailable, use normal polling without repeated connection attempts until the window reloads, the account changes, or this setting is toggled. When disabled, do not request feed credentials or open a feed connection; use normal polling only.

enumDescriptions: Download and install updates automatically only for enabled extensions.
Extensions are not automatically updated.
extensions.autoUpdate.description: Controls the automatic update behavior of extensions. The updates are fetched from a Microsoft online service.

description.value: Controls the automatic update behavior of extensions. The updates are fetched from a Microsoft online service.

enumDescriptions.value: Download and install updates automatically only for enabled extensions.
Extensions are not automatically updated.

extensions.autoUpdateDelay.markdownDescription: Controls the delay in hours after an extension update is published before it is automatically installed. Only applies when `#extensions.autoUpdate#` is set to `on`. This delay helps avoid installing potentially problematic updates immediately after release.

description.value: Controls the delay in hours after an extension update is published before it is automatically installed. Only applies when `#extensions.autoUpdate#` is set to `on`. This delay helps avoid installing potentially problematic updates immediately after release.

extensions.autoCheckUpdates.description: When enabled, automatically checks extensions for updates. If an extension has an update, it is marked as outdated in the Extensions view. The updates are fetched from a Microsoft online service.

extensions.ignoreRecommendations.description: When enabled, the notifications for extension recommendations will not be shown.

extensions.showRecommendationsOnlyOnDema.deprecationMessage: This setting is deprecated. Use extensions.ignoreRecommendations setting to control recommendation notifications. Use Extensions view's visibility actions to hide Recommended view by default.

extensions.closeExtensionDetailsOnViewCh.description: When enabled, editors with extension details will be automatically closed upon navigating away from the Extensions View.

extensions.confirmedUriHandlerExtensionI.description: When an extension is listed here, a confirmation prompt will not be shown when that extension handles a URI.

enumDescriptions: The Web Worker Extension Host will always be launched.
The Web Worker Extension Host will never be launched.
The Web Worker Extension Host will be launched when a web extension needs it.

extensions.supportVirtualWorkspaces.markdownDescription: Override the virtual workspaces support of an extension.

extensions.experimental.affinity.markdownDescription: Configure an extension to execute in a different extension host process.

extensions.supportUntrustedWorkspaces.markdownDescription: Override the untrusted workspace support of an extension. Extensions using `true` will always be enabled. Extensions using `limited` will always be enabled, and the extension will hide functionality that requires trust. Extensions using `false` will only be enabled only when the workspace is trusted.

enumDescriptions: Extension will always be enabled.
Extension will only be enabled only when the workspace is trusted.
Extension will always be enabled, and the extension will hide functionality requiring trust.
supported.description: Defines the untrusted workspace support setting for the extension.

version.description: Defines the version of the extension for which the override should be applied. If not specified, the override will be applied independent of the extension version.

extensions.experimental.deferredStartupF.description: When enabled, extensions which declare the `onStartupFinished` activation event will be activated after a timeout.

extensions.experimental.issueQuickAccess.description: When enabled, extensions can be searched for via Quick Access and report issues from there.

extensions.allowOpenInModalEditor.description: Controls whether extensions and MCP servers open in a modal editor overlay.

extensions.verifySignature.description: When enabled, extensions are verified to be signed before getting installed.

extensions.autoRestart.description: If activated, extensions will automatically restart following an update if the window is not in focus. There can be a data loss if you have open Notebooks or Custom Editors.

extensions.supportNodeGlobalNavigator.description: When enabled, Node.js navigator object is exposed on the global scope.

extensions.requestTimeout.description: Controls the timeout in milliseconds for HTTP requests made when fetching extensions from the Marketplace

inlineChat.defaultModel.description: Select the default language model to use for inline chat from the available providers. Model names may include the provider in parentheses, for example 'Claude Haiku 4.5 (copilot)'.

agents.voice.enabled.description: Enable the Voice Mode panel in the chat view for voice-driven coding conversations.

description.value: Enable the Voice Mode panel in the chat view for voice-driven coding conversations.

agents.voice.showButton.markdownDescription: Controls whether the Voice Mode button is shown in the chat input. When hidden, Voice Mode can still be started with its keyboard shortcut.

agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel.markdownDescription: The OpenAI live model ID to use for Voice Mode with your configured API key. Add the key in Models Management. Voice Mode uses this model when client BYOK is allowed and the key has access to it; leave empty to use the hosted voice model, which requires a paid Copilot plan.

agents.voice.sessionAwareness.markdownDescription: Share a bounded briefing of tracked sessions and the active chat's recent conversation with OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode, so it can answer session status questions directly. This includes session titles, response summaries, pending prompt details, the selected model, and attachment names, but not attachment contents. Disable to restore input-only context. Changes take effect when Voice Mode reconnects.

agents.voice.speakResponses.markdownDescription: When enabled, the assistant reads responses aloud. When disabled, responses are not spoken; enable `#agents.voice.showTranscript#` to read them as a text transcript instead.

agents.voice.agentProgress.markdownDescription: Allow Agent mode to speak brief semantic progress updates while it investigates, plans, edits, validates, or recovers from a problem.

enumDescriptions: Harper.
Birch.
Junho.
Oak.
agents.voice.voice.markdownDescription: The voice used when the assistant reads responses aloud. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately. Use [Voice Mode instructions](command:workbench.action.chat.configureVoiceInstructions) to customize Voice Mode behavior and terminology.

agents.voice.language.markdownDescription: The language used for speech recognition, dictation, and spoken responses. The selectable languages support native voice output. Automatic uses the configured display language for speech recognition and dictation when supported; otherwise, it follows the system or browser locale. English voice output is used when the detected language does not support native voice output. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately.

agents.voice.showTranscript.markdownDescription: Show the voice transcript overlay in the chat input area while voice mode is active. Enable this to read responses as text when `#agents.voice.speakResponses#` is disabled.

agents.voice.liveTranscript.markdownDescription: Show your speech as a live, word-by-word transcript while you are speaking. When disabled, your transcript appears only once you finish speaking. Requires `#agents.voice.showTranscript#` to be enabled to be visible.

agents.voice.handsFree.markdownDescription: When enabled, voice mode automatically re-enters listening after the assistant finishes speaking, so you can hold a hands-free back-and-forth conversation. When disabled, you start and end each turn manually, and ending the turn sends it. Turns are not ended automatically on trailing silence or a stop phrase unless `#agents.voice.turn.silenceMs#` or `#agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases#` is explicitly configured.

agents.voice.turn.silenceMs.markdownDescription: Trailing silence in milliseconds before the backend ends the turn automatically. Set to `-1` to disable ending the turn on silence, in which case the turn ends only via a stop phrase (`#agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases#`) or manually. When enabled, the backend clamps this to its supported range (currently 200-5000 ms) and is the source of truth. When hands-free mode (`#agents.voice.handsFree#`) is disabled, the turn is not ended on silence by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.

anyOf.description: Do not end the turn on trailing silence.

agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases.markdownDescription: Phrases that end the turn when spoken at the end of an utterance. Leave empty to disable ending the turn on a stop phrase, in which case the turn ends only on trailing silence (`#agents.voice.turn.silenceMs#`) or manually. The backend strips the matched phrase from the transcript before it reaches the agent. When hands-free mode (`#agents.voice.handsFree#`) is disabled, stop phrases do not end the turn by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.

interactiveWindow.executeWithShiftEnter.markdownDescription: Execute the Interactive Window (REPL) input box with shift+enter, so that enter can be used to create a newline.

interactiveWindow.showExecutionHint.markdownDescription: Display a hint in the Interactive Window (REPL) input box to indicate how to execute code.

files.autoSaveWhenNoErrors.markdownDescription: When enabled, will limit [auto save](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/codebasics#_save-auto-save) of editors to files that have no errors reported in them at the time the auto save is triggered. files.watcherExclude.markdownDescription: Configure paths or [glob patterns](https://aka.ms/vscode-glob-patterns) to exclude from file watching. Paths can either be relative to the watched folder or absolute. Glob patterns are matched relative from the watched folder. When you experience the file watcher process consuming a lot of CPU, make sure to exclude large folders that are of less interest (such as build output folders).

files.watcherInclude.description: Configure extra paths to watch for changes inside the workspace. By default, all workspace folders will be watched recursively, except for folders that are symbolic links. You can explicitly add absolute or relative paths to support watching folders that are symbolic links. Relative paths will be resolved to an absolute path using the currently opened workspace.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Disable hot exit. A prompt will show when attempting to close a window with editors that have unsaved changes.

Hot exit will be triggered when the last window is closed on Windows/Linux or when the `workbench.action.quit` command is triggered (command palette, keybinding, menu). All windows without folders opened will be restored upon next launch. A list of previously opened windows with unsaved files can be accessed via `File > Open Recent > More...`

Hot exit will be triggered when the last window is closed on Windows/Linux or when the `workbench.action.quit` command is triggered (command palette, keybinding, menu), and also for any window with a folder opened regardless of whether it's the last window. All windows without folders opened will be restored upon next launch. A list of previously opened windows with unsaved files can be accessed via `File > Open Recent > More...`
files.hotExit.markdownDescription: [Hot Exit](https://aka.ms/vscode-hot-exit) controls whether unsaved files are remembered between sessions, allowing the save prompt when exiting the editor to be skipped.

files.readonlyInclude.markdownDescription: Configure paths or [glob patterns](https://aka.ms/vscode-glob-patterns) to mark as read-only. files.readonlyFromPermissions.markdownDescription: Marks files as read-only when their file permissions indicate as such. This can be overridden via `#files.readonlyInclude#` and `#files.readonlyExclude#` settings.

explorer.excludeGitIgnore.markdownDescription: Controls whether entries in .gitignore should be parsed and excluded from the Explorer. Similar to `#files.exclude#`.

explorer.fileNesting.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls whether file nesting is enabled in the Explorer. File nesting allows for related files in a directory to be visually grouped together under a single parent file.

explorer.fileNesting.expand.markdownDescription: Controls whether file nests are automatically expanded. `#explorer.fileNesting.enabled#` must be set for this to take effect.

explorer.fileNesting.patterns.markdownDescription:
Controls nesting of files in the Explorer. `#explorer.fileNesting.enabled#` must be set for this to take effect. Each __Item__ represents a parent pattern and may contain a single `*` character that matches any string. Each __Value__ represents a comma separated list of the child patterns that should be shown nested under a given parent. Child patterns may contain several special tokens:
- `${capture}`: Matches the resolved value of the `*` from the parent pattern
- `${basename}`: Matches the parent file's basename, the `file` in `file.ts`
- `${extname}`: Matches the parent file's extension, the `ts` in `file.ts`
- `${dirname}`: Matches the parent file's directory name, the `src` in `src/file.ts`
- `*`:  Matches any string, may only be used once per child pattern

^[^*]*\\*?[^*]*$.markdownDescription: Each key pattern may contain a single `*` character which will match any string.

Prefix a pattern with `!` to search matching files and folders even if another pattern, including one from `#files.exclude#`, excludes them.

anyOf.markdownDescription:
Map URI pattern to an opener id.
Example patterns: 

- `https://microsoft.com`: Matches this specific domain using https
- `https://microsoft.com:8080`: Matches this specific domain on this port using https
- `https://microsoft.com:*`: Matches this specific domain on any port using https
- `https://microsoft.com/foo`: Matches `https://microsoft.com/foo` and `https://microsoft.com/foo/bar`, but not `https://microsoft.com/foobar` or `https://microsoft.com/bar`
- `https://*.microsoft.com`: Match all domains ending in `microsoft.com` using https
- `microsoft.com`: Match this specific domain using either http or https
- `*.microsoft.com`: Match all domains ending in `microsoft.com` using either http or https
- `http://192.168.0.1`: Matches this specific IP using http
- `http://192.168.0.*`: Matches all IP's with this prefix using http
- `*`: Match all domains using either http or https
